From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes on production (32k requests)

Quick initial triage results (first 20m):
- Observed increased CPU fallbacks for ~32k requests: GPU kernels are hitting KV-cache misses and token beam expands cause kernel selection to flip to a slower codepath.
- Blocked kernels are queuing; we see per-request serialization on CPU-bound fallback which is inflating p99.
- Error rate spike correlates with out-of-memory fallbacks and a new guardrail that returns 5xx on oom after retries.

Attachments: redwood_log_excerpt.txt, kv-cache-heatmap.svg (heatmap shows KV miss clusters at 08:38–08:42).

Short term mitigations we can apply now (low risk):
1) Route 32k requests through a dedicated slower pool with higher memory headroom (reduces throughput but prevents OOM).
2) Enable automatic prefix caching for FinFlux's common prompts to reduce KV misses.
3) Apply a per-customer soft throttle at 20% for the 32k route to reduce queuing while we investigate.

I'll prepare a one-click rollout for option 1 + 3 and post the change window.

— Marcus
VP Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Laura / Marissa — final update from today:
- Timeline: spike detected 08:40 PT, mitigations (throttle + dedicated high-memory pool) deployed at 10:35 PT.
- Impact: p99 dropped from ~4.8s to ~1.2s after mitigation; error rate returned to baseline within 12 minutes.
- Root cause (engineer triage): kernel-selection heuristics for long-context sequences (>=32k) produced cache fragmentation; when misses clustered we fell back to CPU-bound codepath that serialized work and inflated tail latency.
- Next steps: engineering to deliver a runtime patch (improved kernel selection + expanded KV caching) in the next release cycle; PM to produce a prompt-level caching suggestion for FinFlux; CS to negotiate a defined SLA remedy if required.

Exec ask: approve offering FinFlux either a 10% one-time service credit or a 30-day trial of a small Dedicated pool at no charge while we ship the runtime fix. Customer leans toward credits but asked to keep Dedicated as an option.

Please confirm approval to proceed with the credit or authorize the temporary Dedicated offer.

— Hannah
